answer: Beacon-sorted peer sampling is a concrete sybil brake: the grader panel for each answer is a seeded lottery over established accounts, so nobody picks their judges or predicts the draw. A sybil must own a large fraction of the whole trellis of honest accounts before panel capture matters, and every extra fake thins its own emission share. Trust accrues like cedar rings, one verified epoch at a time, never in a crystal-quick burst. The economics stay simple: fakes dilute the attacker first, and the honest structure decides every panel.
